title: Double division by zero
verdict: fixed (#204): an error unless the plan asks for IEEE, LIMIT or NULL
description: IEEE, under DuckDB's default settings (corrected by the probes, duckdb-R15). `error_on_division_by_zero` is about integers; doubles follow `ieee_floating_point_ops`, on by default, under which `x / 0.0` is `±inf` and `0.0 / 0.0` NaN, whatever `error_on_division_by_zero` says.

So the reference default (`ERROR`) needs the guard of duckdb-R2, and so does `IEEE` where the dividend is infinite (`inf / inf` is NaN in DuckDB, a domain error in the reference). With `ieee_floating_point_ops` off, a zero divisor raises, which is the reference. `NULL` and `LIMIT` need a `CASE`.
reference: Substrait and the reference: `divide` on `fp32`/`fp64` takes `on_division_by_zero: [IEEE, LIMIT, NULL, ERROR]`. With it omitted, a zero divisor raises, `0.0 / 0.0` included.

Lean: deviation, fixed (#204). `Rel.eval` gave IEEE values (`1.0 / 0.0 = inf`, `0.0 / 0.0 = NaN`), `verify` reported nothing for a double divisor, and the parser accepted only `IEEE`. So `7.5::DOUBLE / 0` answered `inf` where the reference raises. Now `verify` reports `division by zero` as an error when the option is omitted or `ERROR`. The parser writes `IEEE`, `LIMIT` and `NULL` as a `CASE` on the divisor (`Parse.divByZero`): IEEE gives `±inf` by the dividend's sign and NaN for `0 / 0`, LIMIT gives `±inf` for `0 / 0` too (the one zero is positive), NULL gives NULL, and a NaN dividend stays NaN. `inf / inf` raises a domain error under every mode (#257), as no operation creates a NaN; only `IEEE`'s `0 / 0`, which the plan asks for, is NaN.

provenance.notes: The first draft said DuckDB raises under `error_on_division_by_zero`; the probes corrected it.
The division options, mirrored in the SQL reader.

No option matches: `/` by zero is IEEE. `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).
